name: Prefix/radix-cache hit path: a full cache hit turns a request into pure GEMM with no attention recompute
arithmetic_intensity: This is the case where the KV machinery inverts into a saving rather than a cost. On a full prefix hit of length L_hit, the attention FLOPs for those L_hit positions (the ~2 x L^2 x d x layers term) are not recomputed at all: they were computed once when the prefix was first seen and are now read from HBM. What remains is the GEMM work for the new tokens plus one attention pass whose queries are only the new positions, so the residual cost is decode_gemm + decode_attention rather than prefill_attention + prefill GEMMs. The price is paid in bytes instead of flops: the KV for L_hit tokens must be read from wherever it lives (HBM, DRAM tier, or a remote store), so the hit path converts a compute cost into a bandwidth cost. That inversion is the whole economic argument for prefix caching on workloads with shared prefixes - RAG, multi-turn chat, agent loops, a fixed system prompt - and it is why cache hit rate, not kernel tiling, sets the practical AI of a request.
scales_with: prefix_hit_length (the entire saving: attention flops avoided scale as L_hit^2)
prefix_sharing_rate across requests (a cache that nothing shares is pure overhead)
kv_residency (HBM vs DRAM vs remote determines the bytes-per-second the hit path gets)
kv_cache_layout and block_granularity (a hit must land on a block boundary or be recomputed)
block_table_and_hash_computation cost (per-request, grows with hit length)
workarounds: RadixAttention-style prefix sharing over the KV tree so multi-turn prefixes are stored once (SGLang)
Automatic prefix caching keyed on token-block hashes (vLLM; on by default in v1 for supported models)
Keep the shared prefix resident in GPU HBM rather than in a lower tier - the tier only helps once the hot set fits
Selective recompute only the tokens whose KV came from a non-identical position (CacheBlend, used by LMCache for non-prefix reuse) to bound quality loss
Semantic KV reuse (donor blocks from a different request) is explicitly gated and experimental - TRT-LLM's RFC requires explicit engine support before any non-identical KV is materialized
notes: The engineering trap in this class is that a hit path and a cold path that are not bit-identical produce an output that depends on cache state. vLLM issue #40896 is the clean demonstration with no external tier involved: with prefix caching on, the same request at temperature=0 returns output A on a freshly started server and output B thereafter, and disabling prefix caching makes it deterministic. The stated root causes in the wider issue set are all key-identity gaps, not arithmetic: blocks reused across LoRA adapters sharing a name (#30931), blocks reused across model/input-embedding variants that are omitted from the key, and - the general form - blocks produced under a different numerical configuration (attention backend, batch-invariance mode, GPU architecture) because those fields are not in the offload namespace or the connector compatibility hash (#58263). A reader should treat 'cache hit' as a claim about provenance, not just about tokens: a hit is only valid if every field that changes the produced KV is part of the key.
